content: My name is Nathan. I am a game writer and developer based in Brazil. I make games under the alias of N. Erebus. My work focus on using atmosphere, tone, and gameplay to create unique and cohesive experiences that lingers long after the player closes the game.

Engine: Godot 4 Role: Solo dev Playtime: 10-15 minutes Platforms: Windows
Description#A surreal 3D first-person platformer inspired by FLCL, Twin Peaks, Alice in Wonderland, and a little bit of Radiohead. It follows a powerful child who must bring joy to the villagers of the Village at the Edge of the Universe, so that they can call up their dormant god to take them away.
Design Goals#This game was designed to be played and finished in one sitting while still sticking with the player long after they closed it. To do that, I tried to surprise the player on every section, making sure they could never guess what was coming next.
Challenges#As with my last project, this was also for a game jam. I had eight days to build it, and planned my time accordingly with a buffer period in case something happened. And something did happen. I had a really bad migraine that cost me one day of potential progress. I considered removing one of the later platforming sections to focus on polishing the rest of the game, but after thinking really hard, I realized that removing it would diminish the effect of the ending because of the pacing. In the end, I choose to work really hard on the last few days to make sure that the section in question made the cut.

title: Spin With Me at the Edge of the Universe

content:
Engine: Godot 4 Role: Solo dev ** Playtime: ~5 minutes Platforms: Browser, Windows
Description#This game tells the story of a young boy named Marco and his obsession with attention. It uses gameplay, level design, and sound design to tell that story effectively in a way that matches the protagonist’s personal journey. It was originally written in Brazilian Portuguese, but I later localized it to English.
Design Goals#I wanted to connect narrative and gameplay to enhance the effect of both, creating something that is greater than the sum of its parts.
Challenges#This project was a game jam project, and I had two other people working with me at the start. They had to leave, however, due to personal reasons after the brainstorming phase, meaning I had to do everything else by myself. This meant reducing the scope, and changing the art style to something simpler while keeping the tone and effect intact.
Media#Links#Play it here
title: What Their Eyes Cannot See

Engine: RPG Maker VX Ace Role: Solo dev Playtime: 15-25 minutes Platforms: Windows
Description#A short RPG adventure where you play as a newbie adventurer ready for his first quest – pest control. The quest, however, is not as simple as it seem as one of the clients is missing, and the other is an old man with bad memory.
Design Goals#I wanted to take the simplest adventure premise for a quest I could think of and turn it into a an engaging interactive short story.

content:
Johnny was an unremarkable baby born at the age of zero to even more unremarkable parents. He learned to speak early and seemed very happy about it, his parents, not so much.
Johnny spoke of space and aliens, of robots and spaceships. He asked all the question a child of his age should ask, and a little bit more. His mother tried her best to answer, inventing what she couldn’t. His father didn’t bother. Johnny started to suspect that the adults didn’t know everything.
All that curiosity paid off in school. His grades were good, and the teachers spoke well of him. Maths and sciences were his favourites subjects. He would often bring questions to the teachers about space and the stars. The answer, regardless of the question, would always be the same:
“No need to worry, that won’t be on the test.”
At the age of 13, he met a girl. His grades dropped, but not by much. He wasn’t brave enough to confess, but the idea of seeing her was motivation enough to keep studying hard. Luckily for Johnny, the girl was into smart boys. She was the one to make the move just before high school.
Graduation was in sight, university life was next, but Johnny hadn’t decided on a career path yet. He had too many interests, and it was too hard to choose just one.
“Choose an easy field that pays well.” That was what his father always said. “Don’t dream too big. You’re smart. Only fools dream big.”
During the final days before graduation, the school distributed pamphlets with a list of career paths in alphabetical order, detailing the expected salary and how difficult they are to get into. His girlfriend chose journalism. He chose, after thinking about what his father had said, the first item on the list: architecture.
Years later, he was married with his school sweetheart, and had two children together. He had a job that paid well, and he was decent at it. Not the best, but the most reliable. Many of the buildings in the big city were his. They all looked the same. When colleagues questioned his style choice, he would always say that he was doing what the client asked, nothing more.
Middle age brought some bad news. Cancer, his doctor said, terminal. There was nothing he could do except to wait for the inevitable. He looked back to all his life achievements, finding only a shelf with worthless awards and certificates.
One last client came to him before he closed up shop. Some rich businessman wanting a building the size of his ego. Johnny didn’t care about who he was, but he decided that this last project would be the best thing he had ever done.
“I’ll make you a building that will touch the stars.” Johnny said, shaking his client’s hands.
Johnny grabbed all that he considered important in his office, placing it inside a cardboard box. He left and locked that door for the very last time, the moonlight illuminating the empty room. He looked up to the sky while walking towards his car, noticing the full moon illuminating a rocket ready to explore the vastness of the universe. Tears slid down his face when he realized that that rocket was the silhouette of his “Star Scraper”.
title: The Unremarkable Life of Johnny Mann

content:
Warning: This story contains very graphic depictions of gore and violence
“I don’t like your eyes”. The old man says before leaping on top of the boy. His knees trap the boy’s arms, who screams and jerks trying to get out. No one is there to help him.
The old man brings his dirty fingernails to the boy’s eyes, tapping it and trying to gain purchase, blood and tears covering the child’s face.
“Help! Help! He’s pulling my eye out!” The boy screams, and no one hears.
The right eye pops out of the boy’s skull, dangling by the nerves. The man grins and uses his teeth to cut it off. The boy screams again, and the old man screams back in his face.
“Now the other one.” The eyeball rolls over the grass.
The boy tries to fight back as much as he can, but the old man’s strength is too much. He passes out from shock and pain, leaving the old man disappointed by the lack of resistance.
“What are you doing to my baby!” Screams the woman on the distance, the sound is like needles to the man’s ears.
He raises both of his hands into the air as if surrendering while getting up slowly and shaking his head. Satisfied, he steps on the eye with his boot and walks away towards the woods as if nothing had happened. The mother sprints towards her unconscious child, and the man vanishes never to be seen again.
title: I Don't Like Your Eyes
